samples.summary: Flipping the webhook default to ENFORCE denies the backend's own tokenless Yorkie client, breaking every server-side `withDocument` path
samples.evidence: `YorkieService.withDocument` attaches with `new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:42-55) — no `authTokenInjector`, no backend-minted Yorkie token (nothing in packages/backend/src mints one for itself; `signYorkieToken` is only exposed via `GET /auth/yorkie-token`). With the webhook methods registered as documented (`AttachDocument`, `PushPull`, `Watch`, … — packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573-581), Yorkie calls `POST /internal/yorkie/auth` for those attaches with an empty token; `decide()` runs `verifyYorkieToken('')`, throws, and returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:188-193). Before this change the stock deployment was in shadow mode and those calls were allowed anyway; now the stock deployment enforces, so all 103 `withDocument(...)` call sites — API v1 cells/worksheet/tabs/comments/docs-content/slides controllers, `document-copy.service.ts`, `template.service.ts`, `seed/seed-templates.ts` — fail on any deployment that registers the methods and configures nothing else. The fix belongs on the new default (exempt or authenticate the server-side client), not on each caller.

samples.summary: Several out-of-diff docs and package comments still state that shadow mode is the default and that client-side read-only is therefore the write boundary
samples.evidence: docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode … the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary") and 231-235; docs/design/template-gallery.md:668 ("with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only …"); docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301; docs/design/revision-history.md:504; packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 ("ships in shadow mode by default"); packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413 ("shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`"); packages/frontend/README.md:37 ("must … run with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`"). The notes package's own new file repeats the old contract too (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64: "the webhook allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`"), contradicting packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:1-20 in the same file. Nothing enforces these (nested design docs are unchecked, and only backticked *paths* are checked in top-level ones).

samples.summary: The new share-link note mount hands the notes engine a docs-shaped uploader that *throws*, where the notes contract expects `null` on a handled failure — so a failed upload is silent for anonymous editors
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` is typed `DocsImageUpload = (file: File) => Promise<string>` and rejects on any failure (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:15,40-49). The notes seam is `UploadImage = (file) => Promise<string | null>`, where `null` means "the host already told the user" and a rejection is only console-logged (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:16-26,179-190). The workspace route supplies a handler that catches and toasts (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:208-229); the new shared mount does not, so a share-link editor whose image upload fails (oversized file, 403 on a revoked link, network) sees the placeholder vanish with no message.

samples.summary: Read-only note mounts stop publishing presence, so peers lose viewer carets — a behaviour change for every other client of a shared note
samples.evidence: The live-cursor publisher calls `store.setLocalSelection(...)` at packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:170,172 and packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:82; on a read-only mount those handles are now the neutered proxy (`setLocalSelection` → noop, packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts, plus the frontend wrap at packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:152). Previously a viewer-role share visitor's caret/selection was published through `YorkieNoteStore.setLocalSelection` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:415-437) and rendered on every editor's screen. That presence is now gone for viewers; nothing outside the notes package was updated for it (`UserPresence` still lists them by name, so the loss is caret-only).
searchedFor: grep for caret/presence expectations in docs/design/notes and sharing.md

samples.summary: The shared route now statically imports notes-settings/toolbar wiring the removed code deliberately avoided for chunk-budget reasons
samples.evidence: The deleted comment in shared-document.tsx explicitly refused to import `notes-settings` into this route because "Rollup hoist[s] it — and the notes engine with it — into a shared chunk well past the chunk-size gate". The new `SharedNotesLayout` is imported statically at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:35 and itself imports `@/app/notes/notes-settings` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:8-11), only lazy-loading the toolbar. Whether the per-chunk KB / chunk-count budgets still pass is a build-time property this change reverses knowingly; worth a look if the budget lane is near its limit.
searchedFor: grep for lazy() usage of notes toolbar

verdict.reason: Verified independently. YorkieService.withDocument builds a Yorkie client with only rpcAddr+apiKey and no authTokenInjector/token (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:42-45), then performs attach (line 50) and sync (line 59) — i.e. AttachDocument/PushPull, both documented as registered webhook methods (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573-581). The webhook resolves an absent token via verifyYorkieToken(body?.token ?? '') and returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED on throw (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:190-193, 43-47); jwtService.verify('') throws (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:88-91). Only DetachDocument is unconditionally allowed (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:54,184-186). The default is now enforcing — isYorkieAuthEnforced returns true for anything but the literal 'false' (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22, used at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:121-123), so the shadow-mode allow branch (lines 156-171) that previously let these tokenless calls through is off by default. Nothing in packages/backend/src mints a Yorkie token for the backend's own client (only auth.service.ts:67/76 for HTTP callers; authTokenInjector appears in backend source only in comments and in test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:430,499), and no allowlist or exemption exists for the server-side client. Consequently the many production withDocument call sites (e.g. packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts:88,125,160,194,242; document-copy.service.ts; template.service.ts; template/seed/seed-templates.ts) break on a stock deployment that registers the methods and configures nothing else. This is a behaviour change whose other consumers, invisible in the diff, were not updated — the blast-radius lane, at major severity.
